title: Episodic sparse adapter bank with shared Mirror output basis
hypothesis: For correlated episodic updates, one shared output basis plus per-episode Mirror codes reduces actual adapter-bank payload while preserving episode recall; as private episode variation grows, rank/residual cost erases savings.
physical_object: Shared fixed base executor and episodic adapter output basis
mirror_coordinate: Per-episode coefficients selecting shared output directions

task.metric: Per-episode answer nRMSE and nearest-answer exact recall; cross-episode collision leakage
task.router: Shared exact query-key ID to episode; router bytes charged and fixed across methods

controls: Independent sparse rank-1 episode adapters storing key ID and complete answer vector
Mirror shared output basis rank 4 plus per-episode codes
Native PCA rank-4 shared basis using the identical decoder and address payload
success_gate: At private residual 0 and both episode bank sizes 64/128: mean answer nRMSE <= 0.02, exact recall >= 0.99, complete payload <= 75% of independent adapters, and strict improvement over native PCA in a preregistered metric. Rank-4 quality must be reported across all heterogeneity levels.
failure_gate: Failure to reduce complete bytes at zero private residual; recall/error miss; or exact alias to native PCA without strict Mirror-specific gain. On any failure, keep fresh seeds sealed.
boundaries: No language-model or PA152 reproduction claim
No post-freeze tuning against fresh seeds
Episode router is fixed and shared; routing quality is outside this isolated test
